subject: Request for discretionary uptime relief — proposed tiered concession structure
messages:
From: Ben Wallace <ben@medispark.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency outage — request for reimbursement options

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick triage call earlier. To summarize — our traffic spike on 2028-01-09 triggered sustained latency >2s for a subset of inference routes over a 3 hour window. The issue materially impacted our customer onboarding flows and cost of lost conversions is non-trivial. We filed the SLA claim earlier and attached the incident export and the claim form.

Can you confirm what types of remediation/redress Redwood can provide? Ideally we want a clean path (credits or a temporary discount on committed capacity) we can present to our CFO to close out the incident from a procurement perspective. Our contract (Annex A, uptime tier 99.5%) is explicit about credits, but this feels like a partial degradation and we are willing to discuss a custom arrangement that avoids a protracted dispute.

Attachments: medispark-incident-log.csv; SLA-claim-form.pdf

Best,
Ben Wallace
Head of Platform, MediSpark
ben@medispark.com
---
On Tue, Jan 10, 2028 at 07:45 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Wallace <ben@medispark.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 07:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency outage — request for reimbursement options

Hi Ben — thanks for the note and for sending the artifacts. I pulled the incident timeline and confirmed the window you called out (2028-01-09 21:10–24:30 UTC) where median P95 exceeded our committed thresholds for several endpoints.

We want to make this right without adding friction. Before we talk numbers I want to align internally on an approach we can offer quickly that meets both parties' procurement box-checks.

Proposed path (initial):
- Short-term: offer a one-time credit tied to measured impact (tokens processed during the degradation window) — we can do either a % credit (e.g., 50% of affected-token spend) or a fixed dollar offset.
- Medium-term: if Medispark prefers committed certainty, we can propose an add-on: 1 free month of reserved capacity on your current Dedicated pool + a reduced overage rate (25% off) for the following 2 billing periods.
- Governance: both options are contingent on a final sign-off from Finance/Legal; for the add-on we will require a short amendment to the SOW for auditability.

I copied Marcus (CS lead) and Marissa (Finance) so they can model the impact and confirm the execution steps. If that direction works, Marcus — can you confirm the customer touchpoints and whether the free-month route would be operationally feasible? Marissa — can you sketch the accounting path and whether we can net the credit against Jan invoices?

I can also put together a compact memo for exec review if needed.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Production latency outage — request for reimbursement options

Grace / Marissa —

Quick notes after reviewing the incident artifacts and usage patterns: the affected endpoints are lightweight embedding calls that sit behind MediSpark's ingestion pipeline. A free month of reserved capacity would be feasible from an ops perspective; we can schedule a migration to a temporary capacity slice and expedite routing changes. Customer impact appears high on their onboarding funnel, so a visible concession (free month + overage discount) will likely close the escalation.

Operational caveat: we need a 72-hour lead to provision the temporary reserved pool and to ensure KV cache warmup for latency-sensitive routes.

Marissa — baseline impact estimate attached (proposed-tiered-credit-table.xlsx). I show two structured options:
A) Token-based partial credit = 60% of affected spend during outage (one-time invoice credit)
B) Relief package = 1 month reserved capacity + 25% overage discount for two months + 20% credit on affected invoice.

Which of these is preferable vs. what procurement will accept?

-Marcus

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jan 2028 09:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Production latency outage — request for reimbursement options

Grace / Marcus —

I've run the numbers against our billing system and the two options have different revenue and accounting treatments:
- Option A (60% token credit): one-time contra-revenue entry; simple to process and quick to apply to Jan invoices. Net impact to revenue ~ $42k (estimated).
- Option B (1 month reserved + discounts + partial credit): revenue impact is split across product and services; we would need a short SOW amendment and would amortize the reserved-month revenue differently. Net present cost ~ $55k but has the advantage of locking the customer into a committed renewal cadence.

Given the size of MediSpark and the strategic value (they are in pilot with a broader sales opportunity), my recommendation is Option B if we can get exec approval for the one-off concession. Option A is acceptable if procurement requires a quicker, minimal paperwork route.

I'll need exec sign-off on Option B because of the near-term revenue recognition implications. Karthik — can you review and share whether you can greenlight the proposed relief package as an exception? If you prefer, I can prepare a 1-page approval memo with the financial breakout and suggested contract language for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Production latency outage — request for reimbursement options — Exec approval

Team — reviewed Marissa's breakdown and Marcus's operational notes. I support moving forward with Option B (relief package) under the following guardrails:
1) Limit the concession to the current SOW and renewal window — no permanent price changes without formal renewal paperwork.
2) Scope the temporary reserved capacity to the specific endpoints listed in the incident export; do not expand it automatically.
3) Require a signed SOW amendment and a short-term commitment (minimum 2 months post-relief at current committed capacity) to recoup part of the revenue impact.

Execution steps: Grace, please present Option B to MediSpark as our recommended path (1 month reserved free; 25% overage discount for two billing periods; 20% invoice credit for affected window). Attach the SOW amendment template (I want Legal to review before sending). Marcus — proceed with provisioning timeline but do not provision until Legal signs off on amendment. Marissa — I'll need the approval memo and the accounting entries for the finance ticket.

Marissa, copy me on the final memo. Grace, please close the loop with the customer and request a procurement contact and a PO reference if they accept. If they push for pure invoice credit only, we can fall back to Option A with Finance processing immediately.

Karthik Iyer
VP Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
